area: Cmd+P command palette (open latency, typing, file/content/branch search, jank)

harness.app: ~/Applications/Horus.app built 2026-09-04 12:32 from the current working tree
harness.method: CDP over --remote-debugging-port: Input.dispatchKeyEvent for real key events, in-page MutationObserver + rAF frame log so CDP round-trips are off the critical path, Profiler.start/stop CPU profiles, Network domain for chunk timing
harness.caveat: Sibling agents in this workflow launch/quit the same app; two runs were discarded because the app was killed mid-measurement. All reported numbers reproduced at least twice.

timeline:
COLD FIRST Cmd+P (measured 328-357 ms, the user's 'palette does not open instantly'):
1. t=0 keydown 'Meta' reaches window listener useAppShortcuts.handleKeyDown (App.tsx:215-216) -> preloadCommandPalette() starts import('./CommandPalette') (App.tsx:93-97). ~0 ms.
2. t=+1 keydown 'p' with metaKey -> commandFromEvent -> runCommand('goToFile'|'openCommandPalette') (App.tsx:1007-1012) -> commandPalette.open() (App.tsx:138-145).
3. controllerRef.current is null because warm() only runs in a requestIdleCallback that has not fired yet at ~540 ms (App.tsx:977-983), so open() falls through to mountAndOpen() -> setMounted(true) (App.tsx:124-131). ~0 ms.
4. App re-renders, AppLayout renders <Suspense fallback={null}><CommandPaletteController/></Suspense> (App.tsx:575-595). The React.lazy at App.tsx:98-100 throws, the boundary commits a null fallback and stamps globalMostRecentFallbackTime. ~2 ms.
5. The chunk actually loads in 8 ms (Network: requestWillBeSent 556 ms -> responseReceived 564 ms). Evaluating it costs 23 ms.
6. ~295 ms of nothing. react-dom 19.2.8 throttles the Suspense retry to globalMostRecentFallbackTime + FALLBACK_THROTTLE_MS (300 ms) — react-dom-client.development.js:16688 / :27346. CPU profile of the window: 264 ms idle out of 382 ms.
7. t=+328 retry commits: CommandPaletteController mounts, attach() sees openOnMountRef and calls handle.open() (App.tsx:114-119), CommandPalette mounts, useLayoutEffect calls dialog.showModal() + input.focus() (CommandPalette.tsx:177-184). First frame after that is 34-69 ms because .command-palette gets backdrop-filter: blur(30px) saturate(180%) over a full-window scrim dialog (styles.css:2981-2985, :2137).
WARM Cmd+P (after the idle warm has run): controllerRef is non-null, so open() is just setOpen(true) in the already-mounted controller (CommandPalette.tsx:479-503) -> 9-13 ms end to end.

PER KEYSTROKE (measured 2.4 RepositoryWorkspace renders per character, p50 frame 8.4 ms on a 3026-path repo):
a. input onChange -> updateQuery (CommandPalette.tsx:346-352): setQuery + setActiveIndex(0) urgent, then startTransition(onQueryChange(query)).
b. Urgent render of CommandPalette only: rankPaletteEntries over ~7 command entries + <=5 branches (paletteCommands.ts:46-62) and groupPaletteEntries — well under 0.1 ms. File rows are still the previous ones for this frame (intentional).
c. Transition render in AppLayout: search.changeQuery (useRepositorySearch.ts:59-62) does setQuery + setContentResults([]) — a fresh [] literal, so the state always changes identity.
d. useRepositorySearch recomputes fileResults = rankFilePaths(indexedPaths, deferredQuery, 32, priorityPaths) (useRepositorySearch.ts:54-57) -> 0.25-0.46 ms at 3026 paths, 1.0-2.9 ms at 20k. createFileSearchIndex is not rebuilt because samePathList retains the array identity (snapshotPaths.ts:22-29, App.tsx:876-879).
e. AppLayout recomputes workspaceContentSearch = {query, results} (App.tsx:555-558). Because contentResults is a new [] and query changed, this object is new every keystroke, so memo on AgentSessionLayout (App.tsx:364) fails -> RepositoryWorkspace (RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:1285, memo) fails on the contentSearch prop -> RepositoryDiffPanel -> DiffSurface re-render and recompute searchMarkers (DiffSurface.tsx:367-372).
f. The content-search effect then runs (useRepositorySearch.ts:64-96): setContentResults([]) AGAIN (new array), setSearchingContent(true), an ipcRenderer.send cancelContentSearch to main (preload/index.ts:88 -> index.ts:733 -> repositorySessions.ts:56-59) even when nothing is running, and a 240 ms setTimeout. Those two state writes produce a second AppLayout commit and a second full workspace re-render — hence 2.4 workspace renders per character.
g. CommandPalette re-renders with the new fileResults: searchFileActions rebuilds 12 PaletteAction objects with fresh closures (CommandPalette.tsx:258-272), contentActions 8 more (:274-290), results/groups rebuild (:292-311), all <=30 rows re-render. Keys are stable (file:<path>) so the DOM is reused.
h. 240 ms after the last keystroke the timeout fires, ipcRenderer.invoke('repository:search-content') reaches RepositoryService.searchContent (repository.ts:1691-1786): it kills any active rg, spawns ripgrep --json --fixed-strings --smart-case --max-columns 500 --max-count 20 with the 52 exclusion globs, parses each JSON line on the main-process event loop until MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS=200 (repository.ts:117) then kills the child. Measured 55-130 ms on this repo; end-to-end 271 ms from last keystroke to the Content group appearing.
i. All 200 results are structured-cloned back to the renderer; the palette renders 8 of them (MAX_CONTENT_RESULTS, CommandPalette.tsx:45) and DiffSurface turns the rest into editor markers. contentResults changing identity again -> a third workspace render.
j. Closing the palette calls onQueryChange('') (CommandPalette.tsx:488) -> changeQuery('') -> two more workspace renders.

BACKGROUND LOAD ON THE SAME PATH: RepositoryWatcher debounces filesystem events 80 ms (350 ms for metadata-only) and calls RepositoryService.refresh (repositoryWatcher.ts:243-323, :7-12). refresh() Promise.all's three git commands (repository.ts:1341-1354); the third, `ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard` with 52 exclusion pathspecs, measures 3.442 s wall / 1.943 s user / 1.492 s sys and returns 405 paths. Every tick therefore burns ~3.4 CPU-seconds in a child process while the user types. The snapshot itself is cheap to publish — #visiblePaths caches and returns the same array (repository.ts:1378-1400) and RepositoryWatcher#publish omits `paths` when the reference is unchanged (repositoryWatcher.ts:325-339) — so the 1.9 MB path payload is NOT re-cloned per tick, and the renderer's search index is not rebuilt. On this machine typing stayed smooth (p50 8.4 ms) during a tick, so the git walk is a CPU/battery and refresh-latency problem rather than a direct source of palette jank.

findings.title: First Cmd+P after launch costs ~330 ms of pure React Suspense fallback throttling, not work
findings.mechanism: commandPalette.open() finds controllerRef.current == null (the warm() that pre-mounts the controller is scheduled on requestIdleCallback and has not fired at ~540 ms after launch), so it flips `mounted` and React first renders <Suspense fallback={null}><CommandPaletteController/></Suspense> with a React.lazy that throws. Committing that null fallback stamps react-dom's globalMostRecentFallbackTime; when the 10 KB chunk resolves 8 ms later, react-dom 19.2.8 refuses to commit the retry until globalMostRecentFallbackTime + FALLBACK_THROTTLE_MS (300 ms). The user waits 330 ms while the renderer is idle.
findings.evidence: In-page MutationObserver (CDP off the critical path): 328 ms from the Cmd+P keydown to dialog-in-DOM + open + input focused. Repeats: 355/348/357/334/324/328 ms. Presses 2-8 in the same session: 9/10/10/9/10/9/13 ms. Network domain: CommandPalette-Dr1EGm0G.js requestWillBeSent at 556 ms, responseReceived at 564 ms (8 ms). A control `await import('./assets/PerformanceChart-*.js')` fired from the page at the same instant took 13 ms. CPU profile of the 382 ms window: 264 ms `(idle)`, 78 ms `(program)`, 23 ms evaluating the palette chunk. node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js:27346 `FALLBACK_THROTTLE_MS = 300`, applied at :16688 and :18609.
findings.fix: Stop suspending for the palette. Replace the React.lazy/Suspense pair with the module-store + useSyncExternalStore pattern the codebase already uses for the workspace (src/renderer/src/workspaceBoot.ts:13-61): add `const commandPalette = createModuleStore(() => import('./CommandPalette'))`, render `Controller == null ? null : <Controller .../>` in AppLayout with no Suspense boundary, and call `commandPalette.load()` from mountApp in src/renderer/src/boot.tsx:13-30 next to preloadWorkspaceRoot so the 10 KB chunk is resolved before first paint. Then delete the `mounted`/`warm`/requestIdleCallback machinery (App.tsx:102-158, 977-983): with the module preloaded, mount the controller unconditionally and let its own `open` state gate the dialog. Expected: first Cmd+P drops from ~330 ms to the warm 9-13 ms. Do NOT simply move warm() earlier — it pays the same 300 ms throttle, just invisibly, and still loses the race when the user presses Cmd+P in the first half second.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~320 ms on the first Cmd+P of every launch

findings.title: Empty query lists 7 commands and 1 file; the repository's files are never offered as autocomplete and folders never appear at all
findings.mechanism: With an empty query the palette ranks only [...commandActions, ...recentFileActions]. useRepositorySearch returns [] for fileResults whenever `searching` is false (deferredQuery.trim() === ''), so no repository file is offered until the user types. recentFiles is additionally wiped to [] on every snapshotRoot change (App.tsx:984-986), so after a restore the list contains exactly the one restored selectedPath. Separately, the search index is built from snapshot.paths, which is `git ls-files` output — files only — so a directory can never be a result even when typed in full.
findings.evidence: Measured on a cold restore of materialsx-core-3: `{rows: 8, groups: ['Commands','Files'], titles: ['Open repository','Toggle explorer','Toggle word wrap','Toggle context folding','Toggle terminal','Open folder','Open settings','.DS_Store']}`. createFileSearchIndex (fileSearch.ts:84-91) maps paths 1:1 with no directory synthesis; RepositoryWorkspace already derives directories via getDirectoryPaths (RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:1180) but never passes them to the palette.
findings.fix: (a) In useRepositorySearch.ts:54-57 drop the `!searching` early return and return the first N paths by a cheap recency/priority order when the query is empty — priorityPaths (the review/changed set, already computed at :46-53) first, then recentFiles, then the shortest paths — capped at FILE_SEARCH_RESULT_LIMIT. rankFilePaths already returns score 0 for an empty query (fileSearch.ts:14), so `rankFilePaths(indexedPaths, '', 32, priorityPaths)` gives priority-first ordering for free at 0.25 ms. (b) In CommandPalette.tsx:297-303 render Files above Commands for the empty query. (c) Feed directories into the index: extend createFileSearchIndex to accept a second `directories` list (build it once in useRepositorySearch with the same collectDirectoryPaths helper the workspace uses) and tag IndexedPath with kind 'file'|'directory' so folder rows can use IconFolder and open in the explorer. (d) Persist recentFiles per root (App.tsx:984-986 currently discards them) so a restore starts with a real MRU list.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 0 ms of CPU, but removes the perceived 'palette knows nothing until I type' — the top user complaint for this surface

findings.title: Each palette keystroke re-renders the whole workspace tree ~2.4 times because contentResults is reset to a fresh [] twice per keystroke
findings.line: 59-62 (changeQuery setContentResults([])), 77-78 (effect setContentResults([]) + setSearchingContent(true)); App.tsx:555-558 (workspaceContentSearch useMemo); App.tsx:364 (AgentSessionLayout memo); RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:1285
findings.mechanism: changeQuery writes `setContentResults([])` with a fresh array literal, and the effect at :64-96 writes another fresh `[]` plus setSearchingContent(true) in the same keystroke. Both change state identity, so React commits twice. AppLayout's workspaceContentSearch useMemo depends on search.contentResults and search.query, so it yields a new object on each commit; that new object is passed to AgentSessionLayout, defeating its memo, which cascades to RepositoryWorkspace (memo, contentSearch prop) -> RepositoryDiffPanel -> DiffSurface, whose searchMarkers useMemo is keyed on the contentSearch object identity (DiffSurface.tsx:367-372). This only bites in workspaceView === 'file'; in review ('multi') view workspaceContentSearch is undefined and stable, so memo holds.
findings.evidence: Read the live counter that RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:1298 feeds (reviewMetrics.ts:21-23) through the PerformanceHud diagnostics panel: 'Workspace renders' was 4 before the palette opened, 4 after opening it, and 23 after typing 8 characters — 19 extra renders, 2.375 per keystroke, and 0 for the open itself.
findings.fix: Three independent changes, any of which cuts the cascade: (1) keep a module-level frozen EMPTY_CONTENT_RESULTS array and set that instead of a new [] at useRepositorySearch.ts:61 and :77, so React bails out of the state update when results are already empty; (2) collapse the two writes — move the `setContentResults(EMPTY)/setSearchingContent(true)` out of the effect and do it once inside changeQuery, leaving the effect to only schedule/cancel; (3) stop threading the palette query through the workspace: memoize workspaceContentSearch on the *settled* query (the one the last completed rg used) rather than the live keystroke query, e.g. store `{query, results}` as a single state object written once when results arrive, so the object identity changes at most once per search instead of 3x per keystroke.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~2 workspace re-renders per keystroke removed; ~0.5 ms/keystroke on this 3026-path repo, materially more with a large file open in CodeMirror or a big review mounted

findings.title: The palette's query state lives in AppLayout, so every character re-renders the application shell
findings.mechanism: useRepositorySearch owns `query`, `contentResults` and `searchingContent` and is called at the top of AppLayout, the component that also renders AgentSessionLayout (the entire chrome + workspace) and TerminalDock. A keystroke in a transient overlay therefore re-renders the root of the application tree. React Compiler memoization keeps the cost low today, but it is the structural reason CP-3 can cascade at all: nothing between the input and the workspace can stop the update.
findings.evidence: App.tsx:554 `const search = useRepositorySearch(workspace.snapshot, workspace.setError, workspace.gitWorkflow.repositoryReview)` sits inside `const AppLayout = memo(function AppLayout(view: AppLayoutProps) {` (App.tsx:543) whose JSX at :596-600 renders `<AgentSessionLayout key={agentSessionKey} {...workspace} workspaceContentSearch={workspaceContentSearch} />`. Measured consequence: 19 RepositoryWorkspace renders for 8 keystrokes (CP-3).
findings.fix: Move useRepositorySearch inside CommandPaletteController (or a small provider mounted next to it) so the query/file-result state never reaches AppLayout. The only consumer outside the palette is DiffSurface's search markers; publish those through a tiny external store (useSyncExternalStore) or a dedicated context that DiffSurface subscribes to directly, updated only when a search settles. AppLayout then re-renders zero times per keystroke instead of two.
findings.estimatedGainMs: Removes 2 app-shell renders per keystroke; the guard that makes CP-3 unable to regress

findings.title: Content search ships 200 ripgrep hits over IPC per query to render 8, and re-spawns ripgrep from scratch for every settled query
findings.mechanism: Each settled query spawns a fresh ripgrep, and the main process JSON.parses every emitted line on its event loop until 200 results accumulate, then kills the child. All 200 ContentSearchResult objects (path + line + column + up to a 500-column preview) are structured-cloned to the renderer; the palette displays 8 and DiffSurface turns the handful matching the open file into markers. Process spawn + the 240 ms fixed debounce put a hard ~300 ms floor on the first content result.
findings.evidence: Measured end to end: 181 ms after the last keystroke plus the 90 ms inter-key gap = 271 ms until the Content group appeared. ripgrep with the app's exact argv on materialsx-core-3: 'mat' 129 ms (17,254 JSON lines), 'material' 55 ms, 'import' 54 ms, no-match 'zzqqxx' 54 ms. repository.ts:1723 `if (results.length >= MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS || line.length === 0) return` and :1754 `if (results.length >= MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS) child.kill()`.
findings.fix: (a) Cut MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS to what the two consumers need — 24 for the palette list plus whatever the open file needs; better, pass the currently open path in the request and return `{top: 24, forOpenPath: [...]}` so the marker set stays complete without shipping 200 rows. (b) Make the debounce adaptive: contentSearchScheduler.contentSearchDelay already returns 0 for a paste-sized jump; add a second rule that returns ~90 ms once the query is >= 5 characters, since ripgrep itself only costs 55 ms here. (c) Add `--max-filesize 1M` and `--threads` capped below the core count to the argv at repository.ts:1698-1713 so a content search cannot starve the renderer on a big repository. (d) Optional larger win: keep one long-lived rg process per repository using `--json` with a stdin-driven pattern (or reuse the same child with `--files-from`), removing the spawn cost entirely.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~150 ms off first content result (debounce), ~1.5 KB->0.1 KB payload per query, no main-loop JSON parsing spikes

findings.title: Every keystroke fires a cancelContentSearch IPC to main even when no search is running
findings.mechanism: The effect runs on every `query` change and unconditionally calls window.repository.cancelContentSearch() — once on the short-query branch and once on the search branch — before any search has been scheduled. Each call is an ipcRenderer.send (preload/index.ts:88) handled at index.ts:733 -> repositorySessions.cancelActiveContentSearch() (repositorySessions.ts:56-59) -> RepositoryService.#cancelActiveSearch() (repository.ts:2695-2702), which is a no-op when #activeSearch is null but still increments the cancelled metric and costs a main-process wake-up.
findings.evidence: useRepositorySearch.ts:71 `if (hasSnapshot) window.repository?.cancelContentSearch()` inside the `< CONTENT_SEARCH_MIN_QUERY_LENGTH` branch and :79 `window.repository?.cancelContentSearch()` before the timeout is scheduled; searchContent itself already calls this.#cancelActiveSearch() at repository.ts:1693.
findings.fix: Track whether a search request is actually outstanding (a ref set when the timeout fires and cleared in .finally) and only send the cancel when it is true. searchContent already cancels the previous search on the main side, so the renderer-side cancel is only needed to stop a search the user has abandoned.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~8 needless main-process IPC wake-ups per typed word

findings.title: Every refresh on the palette's data path costs 3.44 s of git walking for 405 paths
findings.mechanism: The third parallel command, `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard -z -- . <52 exclude pathspecs>`, makes git walk the entire working tree including node_modules, .venv and every build directory; the pathspecs only filter the *output*. It gates the whole Promise.all, so open, session restore and every watcher tick (repositoryWatcher.ts:305) take at least 3.4 s and burn ~3.4 CPU-seconds in a child process. During the palette's life that competes with ripgrep and with the renderer for cores, and it is why the first-Cmd+P window (CP-1) sits in the middle of a busy machine.
findings.evidence: Reproduced the lead's timing on ~/Developer/materialx/materialsx-core-3: real 3.442 s, user 1.943 s, sys 1.492 s, 405 paths returned. The sibling commands in the same Promise.all: `ls-files --cached -z` 19 ms, `status --porcelain=v2 --branch -z --untracked-files=all` 48 ms.
findings.fix: Do not ask git to walk ignored files at all on the refresh path. Either (a) drop the third command from refresh() entirely and populate the ignored-but-visible set lazily/in the background after the snapshot is published (the paths are only there so gitignored-but-interesting files appear in the tree and in ⌘P), or (b) replace it with the ripgrep call the folder path already uses — `rg --files --no-require-git --hidden --no-ignore-vcs` with RIPGREP_EXCLUSION_ARGS (repository.ts:304-322) prunes excluded directories during the walk instead of after it, and repository.ts:1402-1418 shows the pattern. Either way keep the existing #visiblePaths buffer cache (repository.ts:1378-1400) so unchanged ticks stay free.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~3.4 s off every open/restore/watcher refresh; removes ~3.4 CPU-seconds of contention per tick

findings.title: The palette's first frame costs 34-69 ms because backdrop-filter: blur(30px) creates a full-window render surface on show
findings.line: 2981-2985 (.command-palette backdrop-filter), 2137 (.command-palette-layer full-viewport dialog with var(--scrim)), 2138-2139 (::backdrop opacity transition + @starting-style)
findings.mechanism: dialog.showModal() promotes the layer to the top layer and the compositor must allocate a backdrop render surface and snapshot everything beneath it to run blur(30px) saturate(180%) for the 620x560 panel. The panel already sits on a 54%-black scrim, so most of the blur is invisible, but the cost is paid on the frame the palette appears.
findings.evidence: rAF frame log across the cold open: [69.3, 0.2, 32.1, 2.3, 4.2] ms; worst frame in the in-page cold-open window 33.8 ms. On the 120 Hz display observed here that is 4-8 dropped frames on the frame the user is looking at. Warm opens (presses 2-8) complete in 9-13 ms with normal frames, i.e. the surface is reused once it exists.
findings.fix: Reduce blur(30px) to blur(12-16px) (the difference is not visible over a 54% scrim) or drop backdrop-filter on .command-palette and rely on the opaque --popover background the reduced-transparency branch at styles.css:2989 already uses. If the glass is wanted, keep the dialog in the DOM permanently (which CP-1's fix does anyway) and add `will-change: backdrop-filter` to .command-palette so the surface is allocated ahead of the first show.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~30-60 ms off the frame the palette appears on

findings.title: Row pointer-enter handlers re-render the whole result list, and rowRefs is never trimmed
findings.mechanism: `onPointerEnter={() => setActiveIndex(index)}` is attached to every row. While typing, the result rows shift under a stationary cursor, so each commit fires pointerenter on whatever row lands under the pointer and schedules another CommandPalette render of all <=30 rows. rowRefs.current is an array indexed by row position that is written on every render and never truncated, so it keeps stale nodes from longer result sets alive.
findings.evidence: CommandPalette.tsx:428-438 attaches both `ref={(node) => { rowRefs.current[index] = node }}` and `onPointerEnter={() => setActiveIndex(index)}` per row; the scrollIntoView effect at :315-319 is correctly guarded by scrollActiveRowRef so it is not a per-keystroke layout read, and keys are stable (`file:<path>`, `content:<path>:<line>:<col>:<i>`) so DOM nodes are reused.
findings.fix: Move selection to one delegated pointermove/pointerover handler on .command-palette-results that reads data-index off event.target.closest('button'), and ignore pointer events until the pointer actually moves (track lastPointerClientX/Y and bail when unchanged) so a re-render under a stationary cursor cannot change the selection. Reset rowRefs.current.length = results.length at the top of the render.
findings.estimatedGainMs: Removes up to one extra 30-row palette render per keystroke when the cursor rests over the list

findings.title: Fuzzy ranking runs on the renderer main thread and is the part that scales badly with repository size
findings.mechanism: rankFilePaths does a full linear scan with a bounded max-heap over every IndexedPath for every keystroke, inside a useDeferredValue render on the main thread. It is comfortably fast at the current repository size but it is O(paths) per character with no prefix/trigram narrowing, so it is what turns into jank on a 50-100k-path monorepo, and it competes with the same thread that has to paint the dropdown.
findings.evidence: Bun benchmark against the real 3026-path list from ~/Library/Application Support/Horus/last-workspace.json: 1-char 0.249 ms, 3-char 0.275 ms, 8-char 0.324 ms, worst-case subsequence 0.461 ms. Synthetic 20,000 paths: 1.519 / 1.679 / 2.107 / 2.942 ms. createFileSearchIndex: 0.468 ms at 3k, 2.983 ms at 20k. Live frame times while typing 'material' on the real repo: p50 8.4 ms, p95 10.2 ms, max 19.3 ms, zero longtask entries — i.e. not a problem today.
findings.fix: Do not rewrite this now; it is not the current bottleneck. When the app needs to handle 50k+ paths, add an incremental narrowing cache (keep the previous query's surviving candidate list and re-rank only those when the new query extends the old one — a strict superset filter that turns most keystrokes into O(previous results)), and only then consider moving createFileSearchIndex + rankFilePaths into a worker. Keep the index build where it is: samePathList (snapshotPaths.ts:22-29) already retains the paths array identity across watcher ticks so the 0.5-3 ms index build does not run per tick.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 0 ms today; prevents 3-15 ms per keystroke on large monorepos

findings.title: Per-render allocations in the palette body: unmemoized PR-selector parsing and full re-tokenizing of every content preview
findings.line: 173-175 (parsePullRequestSelector/paletteFilterQuery on every render), 132-146 (SearchPreview), 258-290 (searchFileActions/contentActions rebuild 20 action objects per keystroke)
findings.mechanism: parsePullRequestSelector runs two regexes per render outside any memo; SearchPreview is memo'd but receives `query`, which changes every keystroke, so all 8 content previews are re-tokenized with a global regex matchAll and re-split for query highlighting (searchPreview.ts:50-63); searchFileActions and contentActions allocate 20 fresh objects with fresh closures per keystroke. Individually tiny, collectively the palette's per-keystroke garbage.
findings.evidence: CommandPalette.tsx:173 `const selector = parsePullRequestSelector(query)` at component scope; :276 `.map((result, index) => ({... run: () => {...}}))`; searchPreview.ts:56 `for (const match of preview.matchAll(pattern))` then :63 `tokens.flatMap((token) => splitQueryMatches(token, normalizedQuery))`. The typing CPU profile shows 163 ms of JS across 2269 ms with no single hot frame, consistent with diffuse allocation rather than one hot loop.
findings.fix: Wrap selector/filterQuery/commandOnly in a single useMemo on `query`.
